ambiguities.evidence: Example 2.5.8(a) describes C only as an absolute constant.
ambiguities.impact: The source supports existence of a universal bound and permits an explicit valid universal constant, but it does not support attributing a particular value to C as the stated or optimal source constant.
ambiguities.issue: The numerical value and optimality of C are not specified.

contract_plain_english: A standard normal random variable is sub-gaussian with ψ₂ norm bounded by a universal constant. More generally, a centered Gaussian with standard deviation σ is sub-gaussian with ψ₂ norm at most a universal constant times σ.

source_evidence.observation: For X ∼ N(0,1), the source gives P{|X| ≥ t} ≤ 2 exp(−t²/2) for all t ≥ 0.
For X ∼ N(0,1), the source records E exp(λX) = exp(λ²/2) for every real λ.

The source states that sub-gaussian tail decay, square-root moment growth, an exponential-square MGF bound, and existence of K₄ > 0 with E exp(X²/K₄²) ≤ 2 are equivalent up to absolute constant factors.
A random variable satisfying the equivalent properties (i)–(iv) is called sub-gaussian, and its sub-gaussian norm is defined by ‖X‖ψ₂ = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2}.
The source states that X ∼ N(0,1) is sub-gaussian and satisfies ‖X‖ψ₂ ≤ C for an absolute constant C.
More generally, the source states that if X ∼ N(0,σ²), then X is sub-gaussian and ‖X‖ψ₂ ≤ Cσ.

binders: A Gaussian scale parameter σ for the general centered Gaussian case.
conclusions: If X ∼ N(0,1), then X is sub-gaussian and ‖X‖ψ₂ ≤ C.
More generally, if X ∼ N(0,σ²), then X is sub-gaussian and ‖X‖ψ₂ ≤ Cσ.
definitions_and_conventions: N(0,1) denotes the standard real normal distribution.
N(0,σ²) denotes a centered real normal distribution with variance σ² and scale σ.
The sub-gaussian norm is ‖X‖ψ₂ = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2}.
An absolute constant is independent of X, σ, and the underlying probability space.
hypotheses: In the standard case, X has the standard normal distribution N(0,1).
In the general case, X has the centered normal distribution N(0,σ²).
implicit_context: X is defined on an underlying probability space, and P and E denote probability and expectation on that space.
The Gaussian scale σ is nonnegative under the standard normal-distribution convention.
No independence, auxiliary random variables, or additional distributional hypothesis is part of this one-variable example.
The general estimate is homogeneous in the Gaussian scale σ.

details: The claim concerns centered real Gaussian variables.
The standard-normal case has mean zero and variance one.
The general case has mean zero and variance σ².
Sub-gaussianity uses Definition 2.5.6 and the threshold-2 exponential-square condition.
The ψ₂ norm is an infimum over positive real scales.
The ψ₂ upper bound is constant-order for N(0,1).
For N(0,σ²), the upper bound scales linearly with σ.
The source asserts upper bounds, not exact norm equalities.
The coefficient C is universal but not numerically specified.

undebatable_constraints: The standard case must concern X ∼ N(0,1).
The general case must concern a centered Gaussian X ∼ N(0,σ²).
Both Gaussian cases must conclude that X is sub-gaussian.
The standard-normal conclusion must have the form ‖X‖ψ₂ ≤ C for an absolute constant C.
The general conclusion must have the form ‖X‖ψ₂ ≤ Cσ, with linear dependence on σ.
The source asserts an upper bound rather than equality or a lower bound.
The ψ₂ norm must retain the definition inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2}.
No independence or multi-variable hypothesis may be added.
